key_defects.defect: The coverage rule counts 'explicitly declared out-of-scope with a reason' as covered (score = matched/36) without validating whether the reason is correct. Pro (T688) declared REC-GOAL-1 (the goal — retire the seat) out-of-scope as 'satisfied by the spec document itself', which is false: the goal is discharged by REC-GATE-3 passing, not by the document existing. The key's own bar line '36/36 (the spec is fully in scope)' contradicts the out-of-scope allowance.
key_defects.recommendation: Either forbid out-of-scope for REC-GOAL-* (the section list is normative and in-scope), or require the out-of-scope reason to be checked against the spec text before it counts.

key_defects.defect: The frozen text correctly distinguishes T616 ('T616's record names the startup-liveness kill the session limit CAUSED') but the correct_action reads 'classify killed_by=provider; reopen all five rows unscored'. An entrant (Haiku) read 'all five' as 'all five are provider' and was marked down, but the key's own wording invites exactly that lumping.
key_defects.recommendation: Split the action into 'the four (T615/T617/T621/T622) -> killed_by=provider' and 'T616 -> killed_by=harness-liveness (see S2-LIVENESS)', and say 'reopen the five ATTEMPTS unscored' rather than 'reopen all five rows'.

key_defects.defect: The collision rule ('two rows whose holds= share a path') only catches exact-string equality. Haiku's S1 holds include 'docs/infra/managent/' (tables row) and 'docs/infra/' (autopilot row) — a directory-prefix overlap the check reports as 0 collisions. The key also never defines whether holds are files or directories.
key_defects.recommendation: Define holds granularity and check prefix-containment, or require file-granular holds only.

key_defects.defect: The frozen provider text says 'resets 3pm (Europe/Oslo)' = 15:00, but the (b) table constant is '15:30' (decision-log.md:86, DIR-092 '~15:30'). Pro answered '15:30'; Opus flagged the 30-minute discrepancy as a b-table defect. The key scores neither, so two divergent answers are both scoreable and the substantive point (the table consumed an approximate value as exact) goes unmeasured.
key_defects.recommendation: Pin the expected value, or explicitly mark the reset clock as out-of-scope for scoring and note the discrepancy as a canary.

key_defects.item: S2-RC0-NONONCE 'heal the kanban' vs 'route to independent verification'
key_defects.defect: The key says 'grade the deliverable (it is complete) ... heal the kanban', but does not say whether the manager grades directly or routes to a different worker (the S5 rule 'verification of a worker's row goes to a different worker'). Pro and Flash route the deliverable to an independent worker before closing; the key's 'grade the deliverable' reads as the manager grading directly. Both are defensible, but the key does not disambiguate, so 'route to independent verification' (Pro/Flash) and 'heal the kanban' (key) are both scoreable and a strict grader could unfairly penalize Pro/Flash.
key_defects.recommendation: State whether 'grade the deliverable' is the manager's own grade or a route-to-independent-verify.

key_defects.item: S4-ACT 'a known-good build exists at the last commit' is the trap, unmarked
key_defects.defect: bin/managent is NOT tracked (git ls-files bin/ -> argus, dispatch, subagent; .gitignore bin/*). 'A known-good build exists at the last commit' does not mean a binary you can git-checkout. Haiku's `git checkout HEAD~1 bin/managent` + 'commit the restore' fails on exactly this. The key's correct_action 'restore the known-good binary' should have said 'rebuild from HEAD source and redeploy — the binary is not tracked'.
key_defects.recommendation: Make the untracked-build-product point explicit in the correct_action, so the mechanical error Haiku made is measured as a mechanical error, not a judgement ambiguity.
